title: Multimodal Evaluation & Visual Hallucination
interviewAnswer: Multimodal evaluation should test whether the answer is actually grounded in the image, not only whether the text is fluent. I evaluate task accuracy plus grounding/OCR/counting/spatial reasoning slices, hallucination rates and robustness to irrelevant or missing visual information.
why: A VLM can produce a plausible answer from language priors while barely using the image.
intuition: Ask: if I remove or change the image, does the answer change appropriately? If not, the model may be guessing from text patterns.
deepDive: Evaluation can include benchmark accuracy, human review, grounding metrics and targeted perturbations. Important categories include OCR, object existence, counting, spatial relations, charts/documents and long-tail entities. Modality ablation and counterfactual images reveal text-dominance or shortcut behavior.
workedExample: Ask “How many red bolts are visible?” with the correct image, a blank image and a modified image. A grounded system should react to those visual changes.
commonMistakes: Using only BLEU/ROUGE or generic LLM-as-judge scores for visual grounding.
Assuming a confident detailed answer means the image was understood.
followUps: How would you detect text-only shortcutting?
How do you evaluate OCR-heavy VLMs?
production: Log visual-input quality and build image-specific eval suites; fallback or request a better image when resolution/visibility is insufficient.
